correctness.rationale: For each triangle (origin, successive vertices), sine law yields the exact either-reflection-or-translation recurrence for opposite corner angles. Strict convexity excludes translations in orders 3,4. In orders at least 5, a global minimum angle must have an incoming reflection, giving all angles > π/2−Δ; any translation would thereafter force successive translations and unbounded cyclic angle growth. Hence all angles and radii are 2-periodic. The cosine-law two-radius reconstruction, positive-turn inequalities, the shoelace area, and the one-variable derivative prove completeness and strict endpoint behavior. The standalone verifier independently tested edges, turns, area and endpoints for integers up to 100; these finite checks supplement but do not replace the all-order proof.
